marie.lifeText1: Marie Bashkirtseff (born Maria Konstantinovna Bashkirtseva) was born on 24 November 1858 in Havrontsi near Poltava, Ukraine, into a family of minor nobility.
marie.lifeText2: When she was two, her parents separated. She traveled across Europe with her mother and relatives — Germany, the Riviera — before settling in Paris. She was privately educated and spoke French, English, Russian, and Italian.
marie.lifeText3: She originally aspired to become an opera singer, but tuberculosis damaged her voice. She died in Paris on 31 October 1884, at just 25 years old. Her tomb at Passy Cemetery is a replica of her studio and is a French historical monument.
marie.artistText1: From 1877 she studied at the Académie Julian in Paris, one of the few schools that accepted women. Her teachers included Tony Robert-Fleury and Jules-Joseph Lefebvre. She exhibited at the Paris Salon from 1880.
marie.artistText2: She created approximately 230 works, most of which were destroyed during World War II. Her most famous paintings — 'The Meeting' and 'In the Studio' — capture urban life with naturalistic precision. She was a student of Jules Bastien-Lepage and a pioneer of urban naturalism.
marie.diaryText1: From age thirteen she kept a diary — 105 notebooks, approximately 19,000 handwritten pages. She wrote primarily in French, but also in Russian, English, and Italian.
marie.diaryText2: After her death, her mother published a heavily censored version (1887). Only in 1995–2005 was the complete text published in 16 volumes by Cercle des Amis de Marie Bashkirtseff.
marie.feminismText1: Marie wrote articles for the feminist newspaper La Citoyenne under the pseudonym 'Pauline Orrel'. She criticized the exclusion of women from the École des Beaux-Arts and the inability to freely visit museums.
marie.feminismQuote: 'I know that I should become somebody; but with skirts — what can one do?'
marie.legacyText1: Her diary influenced generations of writers — Anaïs Nin, Katherine Mansfield, Mary MacLane. Simone de Beauvoir drew on it for The Second Sex.
marie.legacyText2: British Prime Minister William Gladstone called it 'a book without a parallel'. George Bernard Shaw was an admirer.

about.title: A Generous Approach to Marie Bashkirtseff
about.projectIntro: This project makes accessible the complete, unabridged diary of Marie Bashkirtseff (1858–1884) — a Ukrainian noblewoman, painter, and proto-feminist who kept one of the most remarkable intimate documents in history from age thirteen.
about.censorshipHistory: After Marie's premature death from tuberculosis, her mother published the diary heavily censored to protect herself and her family. For a hundred years, the diary was considered one of Those Diaries that shape people's lives — sharing a girl's inner world and values like the importance of education, women's rights, religion...
about.fullEdition: Only in 1995–2005 was the complete version published in 16 volumes by Cercle des Amis de Marie Bashkirtseff. They published it in a limited print run — today it's nearly impossible to find.
about.projectOrigin: The project was created as part of archetypal.cz, where we translate meaningful texts that a commercial approach couldn't deliver. First I discovered the shortened diary, then learned that a full version exists, and then that it's not easy to obtain.
about.yearsOfWork: Several years of spare-time work. It took many hours to obtain the complete diary in electronic form. Now I want to make it accessible to the world.
about.currentStatusText: We're currently in the research and annotation phase — carefully documenting historical context, identifying people and places, and preparing the source material for high-quality translation.
about.translationReady: The AI-assisted translation infrastructure is already operational. Early translations into Czech are in progress, and the system can support additional languages.
about.collaborationStatus: GitHub collaboration is currently private while we establish workflows, but will be opened to contributors soon.
about.visionText: My goal is to help Marie Bashkirtseff's spirit make a comeback. To publish the diary in all languages at once. You click which version (censored/complete/selection) and language you want, and you can read, share paragraphs, paragraph images...
about.aiTranslation: Translations are created using AI, with emphasis on preserving Marie's layers of meaning, unique voice, and period context. If a translation in some language doesn't exist yet, the project includes tools that can generate it and then just fine-tune it by humans.
about.conclusion: Marie's words and spirit for everyone who wants to see them.
about.acknowledgmentsText: Thanks to Cercle des Amis de Marie Bashkirtseff for their work on the complete diary edition — especially Ginette Apostolescu, who transcribed the diary, and Michel Fleury.
about.linkDHDesc: what is DH, how this project fits, invitation to scholars
about.praiseInfluence: Her diary influenced generations of writers — Anaïs Nin, Katherine Mansfield, Mary MacLane. Simone de Beauvoir drew on it for The Second Sex.
about.privacyText: This site has no corporate tracking, no advertising cookies, and no data sold to third parties. We use our own simple analytics to understand which entries are read and how the site is used — nothing more. When you install the app, your reading data stays on your device.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This is a nonprofit scholarly project dedicated to making Marie Bashkirtseff's diary accessible worldwide. We collect as little personal data as possible and never use it for commercial purposes.
privacy.dataCollectedIntro: We collect personal data only when you voluntarily interact with the site:
privacy.dataGoogle: Google profile (name, email, avatar) — only when you voluntarily sign in via Google OAuth
privacy.dataReports: Paragraph reports — translation issue reports you submit as a logged-in user
privacy.dataAnalytics: No tracking cookies — we use Umami analytics, which is cookie-free and collects no personal data
privacy.whyReports: To let readers report translation issues and track their own reports
privacy.whyQuality: To improve translation quality based on reader feedback
privacy.storageSupabase: Data is stored in a self-hosted PostgreSQL database on our own server
privacy.storageRegion: Data is stored in the EU region where possible
privacy.cookiesAuth: Auth session token — stored in browser only after you voluntarily sign in with Google
privacy.cookiesNoTracking: No tracking cookies, no advertising cookies
privacy.cookiesUmami: Umami analytics does not use cookies
privacy.thirdGoogle: Google — OAuth authentication only, no data shared beyond login
privacy.thirdSupabase: Self-hosted PostgreSQL — database for user accounts and reports (no third-party cloud)
privacy.thirdUmami: Umami — privacy-friendly analytics that collects no personal data
privacy.rightsIntro: Under European data protection law, you have the following rights:
